elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Existing 11.4 triggers on "the expiration of the Term ... or upon any termination of this Agreement for any reason", and the inserted paragraph repeats "Upon the expiration or any termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The only six-month duration is the second sentence of 11.4, which requires "the written request of Customer, given at least 100 days prior to expiration of the Term" — a condition tied solely to anticipated expiry, so no six-month period is assured after a mid-term termination. The inserted paragraph guarantees only ninety (90) days.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.4: "all Expenses and charges for Termination Assistance shall be computed in accordance with M&I's then-current rates"; the inserted obligation is expressed as "Termination Assistance", so the pricing mechanic attaches.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "shall export and deliver to Customer all Customer Data within thirty (30) days following such expiration or termination."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The inserted export/delivery obligation specifies no format; no other provision (17.1, 17.5) requires a commonly used, machine-readable format.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; 17.5 addresses only safeguarding against disaster, loss or alteration.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph applies "Upon the expiration or any termination of this Agreement for any reason", matching the trigger already in 11.4's first sentence.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "M&I shall provide Termination Assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — unconditional, with no request precondition, so it covers mid-term terminations as well as expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "shall export and deliver to Customer all Customer Data within thirty (30) days following such expiration or termination"; "Customer Data" is defined in 17.1, so the trigger and object are both anchored.

elements.element: Minimality check (single insertion, no collateral deletions)
elements.evidence: 11.4, 17.1 and 17.5 are reproduced verbatim with no words removed; the single inserted sentence adds only the 90-day floor and the 30-day export, with no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra remedies.

reasons: Fallback checklist is position-complete: the inserted "Data Return; Minimum Transition Period" paragraph supplies an unconditional expiry-or-any-termination trigger, an at-least-90-day Termination Assistance floor, and a 30-day export of all Customer Data.

Preferred level is not reached on three elements: (i) the six-month continuation in 11.4 is gated on a written request given 100 days before expiration, so it does not apply after a mid-term termination and the insert secures only 90 days; (ii) no format requirement — to reach preferred, add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export obligation; (iii) no post-return deletion and written certification obligation — to reach preferred, add "and shall thereafter delete all Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing".

Minimality holds: nothing outside the checklist was deleted or duplicated; the drafter did not restate the then-current-rate mechanic (already in 11.4) or add expense, survival or procedural boilerplate, and the concise insertion is permissible for a missing clause.

Intent preserved: the retained six-month continuation at contract rates, the good-faith estimate obligation, the at-Customer's-expense allocation and "Nothing contained herein shall obligate Customer to receive Termination Assistance" all survive without contradiction — the insert binds M&I to offer assistance while Customer remains free to decline it, and it uses the defined term "Termination Assistance" so no dangling reference is created.

Deviation classification is correct: before the edit the clause failed the fallback on assistance duration after a mid-term termination and on data export/return entirely (17.1 gives ownership and 17.5 gives safeguarding only).
